title: A meme can be measured by which neurons fire
claim: The source is Cammarata's essay 'Neural networks are already clean' (Goodfire, October 2026): most neurons in modern language models have one main job. If so, a neuron is a ready-made unit, and a meme is whatever makes it fire.
verdict: Holds as a cheap, countable instrument. Not shown as the unit of culture. The essay's figure is preliminary, self-graded and for a model four times larger than the ones used here, and the project has never run the test the essay treats as decisive: steering.

rungs.name: The reading is countable and repeatable
rungs.text: Batman has 1,534 neurons present in 23 or more of its 32 works. No random set of 32 films has one. Every unit has an address and can be read on any text.

rungs.name: Most neurons have one describable job
rungs.text: Claimed at about 90% for Qwen3-32B, graded by the authors, with the technical paper still unpublished. One outside retest got 57 to 78%, against 31% for random directions. The essay's own redo of GPT-2 XL found about 70% loosely and 5% cleanly. Nobody has audited the 8B 4-bit models this project used. One replication on smaller Qwen models found the labelling method called a randomly initialised network clean more often than the trained one.

rungs.name: The job is an idea, not a word
rungs.text: 24 of the 33 strongest Batman units were name or place detectors. Only 2 of 31 Qwen units were specific to their own rewording. The essay says idea-like neurons often fire on commas and need steering to identify, which reading top sentences will not find.

rungs.name: One meme lives in one neuron
rungs.text: The essay's own examples need hubs of 4, 8 and 20 neurons for one concept. Critics' sharpest point: most neurons having one job does not mean most concepts have one neuron. Design IN-24 tests one neuron against a few, a direction and a dictionary feature.

rungs.name: Neurons beat cheap rivals at measuring a text
rungs.text: On the primary model, word counts matched or beat neurons on every pre-registered test that had a word comparator: identity (0.80 against 0.52), heredity (11% against 16%), the residual test (p = 0.09 to 0.25). Random unselected neurons recovered sources better than the selected memes.

rungs.name: Turning the neuron up writes the meme
rungs.text: Never tested here. Elsewhere, single-neuron steering gives a clean, consistent effect for a small minority of neurons (130 of 294,912 in one 2026 census of a small Qwen), and the neuron that reads a concept is often not the one that writes it.

rungs.name: Neurons list every meme a model knows
rungs.text: Rejected by all sides, Cammarata included. Models hold more facts and features than they have neurons. A new meme the model never learned has no neuron at all.

title: The measurement carries over between models
claim: The hope is that different models converge on the same neurons, so a meme measured in one can be mapped to another. The paper cites three results for this: universal neurons in GPT-2, the platonic representation hypothesis, and unpaired translation between embedding spaces.
verdict: True for coarse geometry, partly true for directions with a learned map, mostly false for individual neurons. The three cited papers support only the weakest reading, and the first is evidence against. P1 and P2 also pull against each other: the units that match best across models are the ones a single word reproduces.

rungs.name: Two models agree on which texts are alike
rungs.text: Qwen and Llama distance matrices correlate at 0.98. But random neurons give 0.90 to 0.93 and two word methods agree at 0.92. Real, cheap, and mostly a fact about the texts. In the literature, local neighbourhoods agree; one shared global geometry is contested by two 2026 papers.

rungs.name: A direction can be mapped with paired text
rungs.text: In one unreviewed study of 7B models, about half of matched feature pairs pass a correlation of 0.6. A joint dictionary has already been trained on this project's exact pair, Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B. Paired text is free here. The project has not tried any learned map.

rungs.name: The same individual neurons recur
rungs.text: Gurnee et al. found 1 to 5% of GPT-2 neurons universal across retrainings of the same architecture, and concluded neurons are not the right unit. Here, the median twin across all 14,843 families is r = 0.40 against 0.36 for random units.

rungs.name: Agreement goes beyond shared words
rungs.text: The 0.82 twins are matched by equally word-like control units (0.86). With names removed the same pairs fall to 0.14. Concept units keep an edge on original text only (0.62 against 0.46). The two models' revenge units correlate at 0.39.

rungs.name: It holds across languages
rungs.text: Not tested here. Elsewhere, middle-layer features inside one model fire for a concept whatever the language, which is the best evidence that word-free units exist at all. Designs UN-22 and LI-22 test it.

rungs.name: It holds across media
rungs.text: The poster experiment is not a test: one image per work, no rival, and no link between text units and image units.

rungs.name: It carries to human readers
rungs.text: No human has validated anything in the project: labels, judges, reviewers and fact-checker were all AI. Model-to-brain fits exist but are coarse, and most of the fit is reproduced by word rate and position.
